<details class="nhsuk-details">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">Text description of this diagram</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

| Step | Where you are | What you do | What you produce |
|---|--------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | Phase 1 Engagement and scoping | State the decision, the deadline, and the certainty you need. Identify stakeholders. | The decision, the question and the deadline, written for the analyst. |
| 2 | Deciding your assurance level | Score it with the analyst: impact of an error, not difficulty. | The completed Analytical Assurance Decision Tool, and the Business Critical answer recorded either way. |
| 3 | The commissioner Three things only you can do | Securing the time and resource the level requires is yours. | The schedule, with the assurance and the reviewer's time in it. |
| 4 | Phase 2 Design | Confirm it meets your need, and approve the design before work proceeds. | The design and plan, with your approval recorded against it. |
| 5 | Phase 3 Analysis | Stay available, and review any change of design or method. | A decision log entry for anything you changed, and why. |
| 6 | Phase 4 Delivery, communication and sign-off | Confirm it meets your need, apply its limitations, and sign it off for release. | Your sign-off, and the quality assurance statement attached to the output. |
| 7 | Phase 5 Review | Did it inform the decision, is it used, should it be decommissioned? | The review record, kept with the project record. |

: The commissioner's journey, step by step

Step 2 is outlined, with a note: **Business Critical.** Any one impact dimension at 4? If so, go to Business Critical analysis.

A second note, **after the last step:** What review finds is what your next commission should start from.

</div>
</details>
